title: Should You Wait for the Federal Heat Pump Rebate?
desc: Ottawa's heat pump rebate opens in early 2027, and installs from November 1, 2026 can apply. What that means for buying now, and a simple rule for whether to wait.
h1: Should You Wait for the Federal Heat Pump Rebate?
lead: You may be asking whether to hold off on your heat pump. Ottawa has now said that installs from November 1, 2026 can apply once the portal opens, so for most homes there is no reason to wait for the rebate itself. The question is whether the rest of your plan is ready.
sections: What Ottawa has said about timing

The National Heat Pump Rebate pays $10,000 if your after-tax household income is at or below your province's line for your household size, and $2,000 above it. The portal opens in early 2027. Ottawa's Canada.ca page says installs from November 1, 2026 can apply once it opens, and that receipts must be sent within 6 months. The program closes in March 2034. The page also says the rules are still being finalized and can change, and that your rebate is judged on the rules in force on your install date. It says nothing about installs before November 1.

Our page on the National Heat Pump Rebate keeps every confirmed detail in one place, with the date we read each source.
A simple rule: is your system failing, or can you plan?

Because installs from November 1 count, waiting does not protect your rebate. It only delays your savings. That gives you three cases.

  • Your system has failed, or is failing this winter. Install now. Emergency installs count, and you do not have to prove the old system broke down. Use the provincial money that is open today.
  • Your system works but is old. You can plan the install for the best time and best quote. Nothing about the federal rebate says you must wait for the portal.
  • Your system works and gas is cheap where you live. Run your own numbers first. Ottawa itself warns that switching from natural gas may not lower your bills. See heat pump on a natural gas home.
Provincial deadlines to check before you sign

Some provincial offers have dates, which is a reason to check them before you decide.

  • Ontario Home Renovation Savings: the heat pump stream pays $1,250 per ton up to $7,500 for homes heated with electricity, oil, propane or wood, and $500 per ton up to $2,000 for gas homes. You need written pre-approval before the work starts, so you cannot apply afterward.
  • BC Hydro: a heat pump rebate of up to $4,000 for a whole-home heat pump replacing electric heat. The extra $1,000 bonus was for installs finished between August 1 and October 31, 2026 and has ended.

Rules change, so confirm on the program page before you sign. Our BC and Ontario hubs list what each program pays and the date we last read it.
Protect your federal claim when you buy

Ottawa says receipts must show your name and address, the installing company, the make, model and AHRI number, how many heat pumps, and the total project cost, including ductwork and electrical work directly tied to the install. Cheap steps now keep the door open.

  1. Keep the signed quote, the final invoice and proof of payment.
  2. Ask the contractor to list the make, model and AHRI number on the invoice.
  3. Check the model is on the eligible product list (by AHRI number) before you sign. The unit must be sold and installed by an HVAC contractor and heat the whole home.
  4. Photograph the old equipment and the new unit's nameplate.
  5. Do not pay extra for a promise from a contractor about a federal rebate. Nobody can promise it yet, because the portal is not open and rules can change.
How much is the federal rebate worth to you?

It depends on your income. Compare your after-tax household income (line 23600 minus line 43500 on your 2025 return, plus a partner's) with the table on our federal rebate guide, or use the Do I qualify? tool. A sample, with both programs paying in full: an Ontario home on oil with a three-ton heat pump could get $3,750 from Home Renovation Savings ($1,250 times three tons). If the federal rebate stacks and the household is above its line, that adds $2,000 for $5,750. At or below the line it adds up to $10,000 for $13,750. Ottawa says the rebate can be combined with provincial programs. Read our province-by-province guide for each province's rules.
faq: Will the federal heat pump rebate be retroactive?
For installs from November 1, 2026, yes. Ottawa's Canada.ca page says those installs can apply once the portal opens in early 2027. It says nothing about earlier installs.
I installed a heat pump this year. Can I claim?
If you installed on or after November 1, 2026, you can apply once the portal opens, with receipts within 6 months. Ottawa says nothing about earlier installs. Keep every invoice and receipt.
Should I wait if my furnace is old but working?
You do not need to wait for the rebate, because installs from November 1 count. Plan the install, get itemized quotes and check the model is on the eligible product list.
Does the BC Hydro bonus still apply?
No. The extra bonus was for installs finished between August 1 and October 31, 2026. The BC Hydro heat pump rebate itself is still open.
When will the federal portal open?
The government says early 2027 and has not given a date.
